TETHER — Hand-Holding for Followers

Source: https://github.com/Kei-BWV997/TETHER
Reviewed revision: 19e04c23a3dac77c5345b8101d6a94df9895d35f (v1.0.2)

Current build: revision 18 integrates offset movement and the physics grip
after a native WWM close approach and ticketed handoff. Ordinary formation
movement retains the following rollback baseline and subsequent cell fix.
Revision 12 remains a withdrawn historical experiment.

Walk With Me adapts the physics hand connection sequence from TetherController.cpp
and distance-based movement speed interpolation from GetSpeedMultiplierFor.
Its existing travel speed hook also references TETHER's SpeedHook.cpp call site.
Adapted files: src/hand_holding_tether.cpp, include/tether_session.h,
src/travel_speed.cpp, package/Scripts/Source/WayfarerTether.psc.

Walk With Me modifications: checked sequential physics operations, cancellation
and rollback, current-skeleton validation, either-side grip, existing companion
selection and eligibility, ordinary WWM travel followed by KeepOffsetFromActor,
ticketed alias cleanup, settled contact, failed-attempt rearming, one shared
speed hook, dialogue grace and bounded acquisition. Revision 16 adds temporary
package arrival tolerances and bounded pre-physics facing after handoff.
Revision 17 uses upstream's fixed 5-unit local-Z palm pivots, prioritizes serialized
alias cleanup and removes a duplicate settling delay. No handholding speed
multipliers are used. The
distance-based speed helper remains as source provenance, unused at runtime.

Revision 18 remembers completed script cleanup while the engine changes package,
adds WWM-authored arm/wrist/finger rotations through OAR, and uses palm-surface
pivots (0,-2.35,5). The local test clips retain containers extracted from this
user's installed Skyrim. They are not TETHER assets or covered by its MIT license;
the public 0.2.0 downloads contain the generator and authored rotations instead.
Players generate those clips locally from their own game files.

Upstream credits asdsad121 for enabling living-actor constraints by first adding
the ragdoll bodies to the physics world, and TESFAN for the movement-speed hook
pattern. These references are acknowledged as technical provenance; their source
files were not copied into this adaptation.

No TETHER HKX assets or NetImmerseUtils.h are incorporated. The OAR SDK is
sourced separately from Ersh and carries its own notices.
The GitHub repository contains no HKX animation files. Its release placeholders
have separate Gulan0 provenance and are not included or relicensed here.
The standalone TETHER plugin is not required. This adaptation is maintained by
Walk With Me; it does not imply KEI997's endorsement or support.
